description: Four dynamics stages on one stereo signal, in series: a noise gate, an expander, a compressor and a limiter, sharing one gain

params.text: Sets how fast the expander and compressor change gain, from 1ms to 2.6 seconds
Sets how fast the gain returns once the signal falls back, from 1ms to 5 seconds
Sets how hard the signal is held back above the compressor threshold, from no compression at one end to ten to one at the other
Sets how steeply the signal is pushed down below the expander threshold, from no expansion at one end to four decibels out for every one in at the other
Sets the ceiling the signal is never allowed past, from -15dB to 7.5dB
Sets the level above which the signal is held back, from -70dB to 7.5dB
Sets the level below which the signal is pushed further down, from -70dB to 7.5dB
Sets the level below which the signal is silenced outright, from -70dB to 7.5dB; at its lowest setting the gate is off
Sets the window the expander and compressor measure over, from 1ms to 350ms; a long window follows the average level and a short one follows the shape of each note
Sets how fast the limiter catches a peak, from 0.1ms to 2ms
Multiplies the signal after all four stages, from 0dB to 20dB
Rounds the corner at both the expander and the compressor thresholds, from a hard corner at one end to 10dB of rounding at the other

inputs.text: One side of the stereo pair to be processed
One side of the stereo pair to be processed
Sets the noise gate threshold from its own voltage instead of from the knob: the size of the voltage is read as a level, the knob is moved to match and 0V is taken as -70dB
Sets the expander threshold from its own voltage instead of from the knob: the size of the voltage is read as a level, the knob is moved to match and 0V is taken as -70dB
Sets the compressor threshold from its own voltage instead of from the knob: the size of the voltage is read as a level, the knob is moved to match and 0V is taken as -70dB
Sets the limiter ceiling from its own voltage instead of from the knob: the size of the voltage is read as a level, the knob is moved to match and 0V is taken as -15dB
Patching either sidechain jack switches detection away from the programme, so the gain follows what is here rather than what is being processed
Patching either sidechain jack switches detection away from the programme, so the gain follows what is here rather than what is being processed

outputs.text: That side of the pair after all four stages and the makeup gain
That side of the pair after all four stages and the makeup gain

notes: the five small lamps show which stage has the gain: yellow for the noise gate, green for the expander, blue for unity, a second green for the compressor and red for the limiter.
two of the small lamps at half brightness mean the signal is inside a rounded corner between two stages.
the two sides share one gain, so a peak on either channel ducks both and the stereo image does not shift.
the limiter follows the peak level while the expander and compressor follow the averaged level, which is why they have separate timing knobs.
the signal is delayed by four milliseconds so that the gain is already moving when a peak arrives; everything through this module comes out that much late.
the four columns of lamps are levels: input left, input right, output left and output right, each covering 22.5dB in fifteen steps.
mono per side: a polyphonic cable is read as its first channel.
the maker's own comments mark this module as superseded by Non, which is the limiter alone with a lower attack floor and a fixed lookahead.
